currentConcept.role: current concept: read three-letter blends and blend/segment up to six sounds in a closed syllable
currentConcept.notes: Introductory and ongoing concept. Each consonant in the three-letter blend retains its own sound; examples in the source sequence include trap→strap, scrap, and script.

currentConcept.role: current concept: read three-letter-blend words with suffix -s or -es
currentConcept.notes: The Step Instruction explicitly practices sprint-sprints and splash-splashes after the initial blend work.

currentConcept.role: subsequent concept: read common closed-syllable Latin-base elements ending in the ct blend
currentConcept.notes: Subsequent Lessons concept. Fifteen source-listed bases: -dict-, -duct-, -fect-, -flect-, -flict-, -ject-, -lect-, -pact-, -rect-, -sect-, -spect-, -struct-, -tact-, -tract-, -vict-.

sourceOrderedTeachingSequence.notes: No new letter-sounds. Teach three-letter blends and up to six sounds first, then -s/-es forms and marking. Add 2.5 nonsense-word reading when ready. Closed-syllable Latin bases with ct are explicitly Subsequent Lessons.

No new sounds in Part 6. Spell three-letter-blend words first with blank tiles, reinforce c for /k/ in a three-letter blend, then add suffix/nonsense spelling once proficient. Latin-base spelling is Subsequent Lessons.

soundInventoryRefs.role: all previously taught vowel Letter-Sound Cards plus selected previously taught consonant and welded sounds
soundInventoryRefs.notes: The Step Instruction explicitly states that there are no new letter-sounds/sounds in Substep 2.5.

wordElementRefs.role: previously taught suffixes plus 2.5 Latin-base elements after those bases have been introduced
wordElementRefs.notes: Do not include the ct Latin bases in Part 3 or Part 6 before their Subsequent Lessons introduction.

selectionRules: Drill all previously taught vowel Letter-Sound Cards.
Be selective with previously taught consonant and welded cards.
There are no new letter-sounds in 2.5.

contentRefs.role: Introductory and ongoing reading instruction for three-letter blends, up to six sounds, suffix -s/-es, and marking
Subsequent reading instruction for fifteen closed-syllable Latin bases ending in ct

selectionRules: Begin with 3-4 actual 2.4 review words.
For an Introduction lesson, teach three-letter blends/up to six sounds before the Latin-base material.
Use the source sequence trap→strap, then additional three-letter-blend examples such as scrap and six-sound script.
Practice suffix -s/-es and three-letter-blend marking after the core blend concept.
Introduce the fifteen ct Latin bases only in Subsequent Lessons.

contentRefs.role: current Word Card routine and Latin-base Syllable Cards after introduction

selectionRules: Begin with the existing previous-Substep fat stack; do not fabricate it.
Use current 2.5 Word Cards only for concepts already taught at that point in the source sequence.
After the ct Latin bases have been introduced, add their Latin-base Syllable Cards and read a separate taught Word Element packet as needed.
Review the complete current 2.5 HFW set plus prior unmastered HFWs.

contentRefs.role: 2.5 three-letter-blend, suffix, nonsense-word, and Latin-base wordlists
Part 4 practice/charting procedure and list types

selectionRules: Practice with 5-6 words from one current-substep list that reflects the instruction for that day.
For charting, use another current-substep list that also reflects the day's instruction and have the student read 15 words.
The source explicitly provides three-letter-blend, +suffix, nonsense-word, and Latin-base lists.
2.5 nonsense words may require tapping and should not be pushed for speed before accuracy.
Use the exact current sentence page reflecting the concepts taught so far and embed all 10 sentences.
Review HFWs/untaught words at the top of the selected page as needed.
Weave questions about current and previous concepts, vocabulary/meaning, phrasing, and word structure.
Use selected previously taught vowel, consonant, and welded phonemes; there are no new sounds in 2.5.
After the Latin-base elements are taught, include selected taught word elements as needed.

contentRefs.role: Introductory and ongoing spelling instruction for three-letter blends, suffixes, and nonsense words
Subsequent spelling instruction for closed-syllable Latin bases with ct

contentRefs.locator: PDF-p-46 / printed-p-42: Ways to Spell /k/ — use c in a three-letter blend, example scrap

selectionRules: Begin with 3-4 actual 2.4 words before current 2.5 spelling work.
Use blank tiles to segment/spell current three-letter-blend words, including source examples string and splash.
Reinforce that /k/ in a three-letter blend is spelled with c, with source examples scrap and scrub.
Only after proficiency with 2.5 real words, add 2.5 suffix and nonsense-word spelling.
Teach ct Latin-base spelling in Subsequent Lessons after those bases have been introduced in Part 2.
